prompt: Only 1 in 1,000 transactions is fraud, so a model that always says 'not fraud' scores 99.9% accuracy.
why: With 999 of every 1,000 transactions honest, saying 'not fraud' every time is 99.9% accurate and catches nothing. Rare classes make accuracy misleading.
trap: The model isn't memorizing; it's ignoring the rare class.

prompt: A rare disease appears in 2% of scans, and the model rarely catches it despite high accuracy.
why: With the disease in only 2% of scans, a model can look accurate by mostly saying 'healthy' and still miss most cases. That's class imbalance.
trap: It's about a rare outcome, not an under-represented group of people.

prompt: The team adds more examples of the rare class so the model sees enough of them.
tells: more examples of the rare class
why: The model barely saw the rare class, so the team adds more examples of it. Rebalancing is a fix for imbalanced classes.
trap: It's about outcomes, not groups of people.

prompt: Defective parts are 1 in 500; accuracy looks great but defects slip through.
why: Defects are 1 in 500, so a model that misses them all still looks about 99.8% accurate. Accuracy hides failure on rare classes.

prompt: The team switches from accuracy to recall because the positive class is rare.
why: Recall asks how many of the rare positives were caught, which accuracy hides when positives are rare. Choosing better measures is how you handle imbalance.
trap: Nothing is wrong with the split.
